key_insight: The paper frames autonomous model discovery by coding agents as a stochastic process that should be evaluated with experimental design, not single-run benchmarks, to measure variability, cost, and quality tradeoffs.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a principled way to compare agentic coding systems like Codex and Claude Code under controlled factors, helping tune reasoning effort for better utility-aware performance.
method: Treat agents as stochastic model-discovery operators mapping discovery data plus an optimization target to a fitted model.
Run controlled experiments across reasoning effort, task, optimization metric, and training-data composition.

Fit regression and inference models for multiple outcomes, including quality, dollar cost, wall-clock time, and process complexity; use canonical decomposition to compare effort direction vs utility direction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a testbed on networked word-forming games, evaluating multiple agent-task-metric combinations with regression-based inference on output quality, cost, time, and complexity.
watch_item: Results may be testbed-specific, so utility alignment and effort effects should be validated on broader real-world discovery tasks before generalizing.
paper_title: An Experimental Design Approach to Evaluating Agentic AI's Autonomous Model Discovery
